memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: " Truthful lips endure forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment."(Proverbs 12:17)

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
I have just seen an apologetic campaign by Zakir Naik, and the opponent was a polite young man named Mahesh. Mahesh asked a single, simple question: "How far are you confident about the truth about Islam?" Mr. Zakir answered that he is very confident, but then questioned Mahesh repeatedly and never actually explained how or why he was confident. By using distracting and trapping questions, he deviated and left Mahesh with his original question unanswered. It is very sad and so upset.
​In conversations and debates about faith, it is easy to become entangled in rhetorical tactics, defensive postures, or circular arguments designed to deflect rather than seek genuine understanding. True dialogue requires a commitment to honesty, listening, and transparency. When we pursue truth, we do not need to rely on linguistic traps or avoidance; rather, we can stand firmly in authenticity, grace, and clarity.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: "Integrity is telling myself the truth. And honesty is telling the truth to other people."  Spencer Johnson

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Heavenly Father, grant us discernment to recognize truth and the courage to speak with integrity and love. Keep our hearts humble in dialogue, that we may always seek understanding and reflect Your light to those around us. In Your name, we pray. Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: Stay grounded in your convictions, and always approach discussions with a spirit of grace, patience, and unwavering truth.
